question: What does section 4 of the Income Tax Ordinance impose tax on, and at which rates?
reference_answer: Income tax is imposed for each tax year on every person who has taxable income for the year, at the rates in Division I or II of Part I of the First Schedule; tax credits are then subtracted from the resulting amount.

question: At what rate is the surcharge under section 4AB charged, and above what level of taxable income?
reference_answer: Individuals and associations of persons pay a surcharge of ten percent of the income tax under Division I of Part I of the First Schedule where taxable income exceeds Rs. 10 million.

question: Does a salaried individual earning more than Rs. 10 million have to pay the section 4AB surcharge?
reference_answer: No. The proviso to section 4AB says no surcharge is payable by an individual deriving income chargeable under the head 'Salary'.

question: From which tax year is super tax on high earning persons imposed under section 4C?
reference_answer: Super tax under section 4C is imposed for tax year 2022 and onwards at the rates in Division IIB of Part I of the First Schedule.

question: What is the super tax rate for a banking company whose income exceeds Rs. 150 million?
reference_answer: 10% of the income (Division IIB, Part I, First Schedule, serial 1), levied under section 4C.

question: What super tax rate applies to a person other than a bank, a fertilizer seller or a Fifth Schedule person whose income exceeds Rs. 500 million?
reference_answer: 8% of the income (Division IIB, Part I, First Schedule, serial 4).

question: How is tax on dividends computed under section 5?
reference_answer: By applying the rate in Division III of Part I of the First Schedule to the gross amount of the dividend; the section does not apply to exempt dividends.

question: Does the separate tax on profit on debt under section 7B apply if my profit on debt exceeds Rs. 5 million?
reference_answer: No. Section 7B does not apply to profit on debt that is exempt or that exceeds five million rupees.

question: How is taxable income defined in the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: Taxable income is the person's total income for the tax year under clause (a) of section 10 (income under all heads of income), reduced (but not below zero) by the total of the person's deductible allowances for the year under Part IX of the same Chapter of the Ordinance.

question: What are the heads of income under the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: Salary; Income from Property; Income from Business; Capital Gains; and Income from Other Sources.

question: Are overtime payments and bonuses part of salary for income tax purposes?
reference_answer: Yes. Salary includes pay, wages and other remuneration such as leave pay, overtime, bonus, commission, fees, gratuity and work-condition supplements.

question: Is a fixed monthly travel or rent allowance paid by my employer included in my salary?
reference_answer: Yes. Allowances such as cost of living, rent, utilities, education, entertainment or travel are salary; only allowances solely expended in performing duties are excluded, and a fixed monthly allowance or one not wholly spent on behalf of the employer does not count as solely expended.

question: How is a car provided by an employer for an employee's private use taxed?
reference_answer: Section 13(3) adds a prescribed amount to salary; under rule 5 it is 5% (partly personal, partly official use) or 10% (personal use only) of the employer's cost of the vehicle, or of its fair market value at the start of the lease if leased.

question: What counts as 'rent' under section 15 of the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: Any amount received or receivable by the owner of land or a building for the use or occupation (or right to use or occupy) of it, including a forfeited deposit under a contract for sale of land or a building.

question: Is agricultural income taxable under the federal Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: No. Agricultural income, such as rent or revenue from land in Pakistan used for agricultural purposes, is exempt under section 41.

question: Is a scholarship received to pay for my education taxable?
reference_answer: No, a scholarship granted to meet the cost of education is exempt, unless it is paid directly or indirectly by an associate.

question: Is support money received by a spouse under an agreement to live apart taxable?
reference_answer: No. Income received by a spouse as support payment under an agreement to live apart is exempt.

question: For how long is the foreign-source income of a returning Pakistani expatriate exempt?
reference_answer: It is exempt in the tax year the citizen becomes a resident and in the following tax year, provided the person was not resident in any of the four preceding tax years.

question: When is the foreign-source income of a short-term resident individual exempt?
reference_answer: When the individual is resident solely because of employment and is present in Pakistan for no more than three years; it does not apply to income from a business established in Pakistan or to foreign-source income brought into or received in Pakistan.

question: For how many years can an unabsorbed business loss be carried forward?
reference_answer: A business loss not set off can be carried forward against business income, but not to more than six tax years immediately succeeding the year in which the loss was first computed (section 57(2)). Longer periods apply to specific cases: eight years for a resident company in the hotel business (losses for a tax year commencing on or after 1 July 2020), and ten years for Pakistan International Airlines Corporation Limited (losses from 1 January 2017) and for the approved Federal Government-owned banking company in section 57(2A).

question: Can I set off a capital loss against my salary income?
reference_answer: No. A capital loss cannot be set off against income under any other head; it is carried forward and set off only against capital gains of later years.

question: Can I claim Zakat paid as a deduction, and can unused Zakat be carried forward?
reference_answer: Zakat paid under the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980 is a deductible allowance; any part that cannot be deducted in the year is not refunded or carried forward or back.

question: Who can claim the deductible allowance for children's tuition fee, and how much?
reference_answer: An individual with taxable income below Rs. 1.5 million; the allowance is the lesser of 5% of tuition fee paid, 25% of taxable income, and Rs. 60,000 multiplied by the number of children.

question: Is Workers' Welfare Fund paid by a business deductible?
reference_answer: Yes. Workers' Welfare Fund paid under the 1971 Ordinance or a provincial WWF law is a deductible allowance (not for amounts paid to Provinces by a trans-provincial establishment).

question: Do I get a tax benefit for donating to a public university?
reference_answer: Yes. Donations to a board of education or a university established under Federal or Provincial law qualify for a tax credit under section 61, computed by formula.

question: Who is entitled to a tax credit for contributions to an approved pension fund?
reference_answer: An eligible person (section 2(19A)) with salary or business income who contributes to an approved pension fund under the Voluntary Pension System Rules, 2005.

question: Is there a tax credit for profit paid on a housing loan?
reference_answer: Yes. An individual gets a tax credit for profit on debt paid on a loan from a scheduled bank or other specified lender used to construct or acquire one personal house within the section's limits.

question: What is the 'tax year' under the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: A twelve-month period ending on 30 June (the normal tax year), named after the calendar year in which that date falls.

question: How many days must an individual be present in Pakistan to be a resident individual?
reference_answer: 183 days or more in the tax year, in one or more periods (section 82(a)). Presence is only one of the tests: an individual is also a resident individual if he or she is an employee or official of the Federal Government or a Provincial Government posted abroad in the tax year (section 82(c)), or is a citizen of Pakistan who is not present in any other country for more than 182 days in the tax year or is not a resident taxpayer of any other country (section 82(d)).

question: Can a Pakistani citizen who spends much of the year abroad still be a resident individual?
reference_answer: Yes. A citizen of Pakistan is a resident individual if he or she is not present in any other country for more than 182 days in the tax year, or is not a resident taxpayer of any other country (section 82(d)). The other tests also apply: presence in Pakistan for 183 days or more in the tax year (section 82(a)), or being an employee or official of the Federal Government or a Provincial Government posted abroad in the tax year (section 82(c)).

question: When is a company treated as a resident company?
reference_answer: If it is incorporated under Pakistani law, its control and management is wholly in Pakistan at any time in the year, or it is a Provincial Government or Local Government.

question: Is foreign salary received by a resident individual taxed in Pakistan if tax was already paid abroad?
reference_answer: It is exempt if foreign income tax was paid on it, e.g. withheld by the employer and paid to the foreign country's revenue authority.

question: How much foreign tax credit is allowed on foreign-source income?
reference_answer: The lesser of the foreign income tax paid and the Pakistan tax payable on that income.

question: When is salary Pakistan-source income?
reference_answer: When it is from employment exercised in Pakistan (wherever paid), or when it is paid by the Federal, a Provincial or a Local Government wherever the employment is exercised.

question: What happens if I cannot explain the source of an investment or money I own?
reference_answer: If no explanation is offered, or the Commissioner finds it unsatisfactory, the unexplained amount is included in the person's income chargeable to tax.

question: Which persons are covered by minimum tax under section 113?
reference_answer: Resident companies, permanent establishments of non-resident companies, and individuals and AOPs with turnover of Rs. 100 million or more in tax year 2017 or later.

question: Who is required to file an income tax return?
reference_answer: Section 114(1) lists several groups, so this is a summary of the main ones: (a) every company; (ab) every other person whose taxable income exceeds the maximum amount not chargeable to tax; (ac) non-profit organizations; (ae) every person whose income is subject to final taxation; (b) any other person who, among other things, was charged to tax in either of the two preceding tax years, claims a loss carried forward, owns immovable property of 500 square yards or more (or a flat in the specified urban areas, or a flat of 2,000 square feet or more in a rating area), owns a motor vehicle above 1000 CC, has obtained a National Tax Number, holds a commercial or industrial electricity connection with an annual bill above Rs. 500,000, is a resident registered with a chamber of commerce, trade or business association, market committee or professional body, or is a resident individual required to file a foreign income and assets statement under section 116A; and (c) persons notified by the Board. Under section 114(1A), an individual whose income from business exceeds Rs. 300,000 but not Rs. 400,000 must also file.

question: If I own a house on a plot of 500 square yards, do I have to file a tax return even with no taxable income?
reference_answer: Yes, as a rule. Section 114(1)(b) requires a return from a person who owns immovable property with a land area of 500 square yards or more in the specified areas, even without taxable income. Exception: under section 115(3) a widow, an orphan below twenty-five years, a disabled person, and (for owning immovable property) a non-resident person need not file solely because of that property.

question: Does a widow who owns a 500 square yard house have to file a return only because of that property?
reference_answer: No. Section 115(3) exempts a widow, an orphan under 25, a disabled person, and (for property) a non-resident from filing solely because of those property clauses of section 114.

question: Who has to file a foreign income and assets statement?
reference_answer: A resident individual with foreign income of at least USD 10,000 or foreign assets worth at least USD 100,000.

question: What can the Commissioner ask for in a wealth statement?
reference_answer: By notice, an individual's total assets and liabilities (including foreign ones) and those of the spouse, minor children and other dependents as of the dates specified; assets transferred to other persons and the consideration; the total expenditures of the person and dependents for the period specified; and the reconciliation statement of wealth (section 116(1)(a)-(e)).

question: What is the due date for a salaried individual to file the income tax return?
reference_answer: On or before 30 September following the end of the tax year.

question: By when must a company whose tax year ends between 1 January and 30 June file its return?
reference_answer: On or before 31 December following the end of the tax year.

question: If my salary income is Rs. 500,000 or more, how must I file my return?
reference_answer: Electronically in the prescribed form, with proof of tax deducted or paid and the wealth statement (and foreign income and assets statement if applicable).

question: How can I get more time to file my income tax return?
reference_answer: Apply in writing to the Commissioner for an extension, by the due date for filing the return. The Commissioner may grant it if satisfied that the delay is due to absence from Pakistan, sickness or other misadventure, or any other reasonable cause, normally for not more than fifteen days unless there are exceptional circumstances. If the Commissioner has not granted an extension, the Chief Commissioner may, on the taxpayer's application, grant an extension or further extension (proviso to section 119(4)).

question: When is a filed return treated as an assessment order?
reference_answer: When a complete return is furnished, the Commissioner is taken to have made an assessment and the return is treated as an assessment order.

question: How long does the Commissioner have to amend an assessment?
reference_answer: No amendment under section 122(1) after five years from the end of the financial year in which the assessment order was issued or treated as issued (section 122(2)). Once amended, the Commissioner may further amend the original assessment within the later of five years from the end of the financial year of the original assessment order and one year from the end of the financial year of the amended assessment order (section 122(4)).

question: What is the deadline to appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against an order of the Commissioner (Appeals)?
reference_answer: Within thirty days of receiving the order.

question: Can a State-Owned Enterprise appeal to the Commissioner (Appeals) under section 127?
reference_answer: No. Section 127(1) allows any person other than a State-Owned Enterprise to appeal the listed orders.

question: When is income tax on my taxable income due for payment?
reference_answer: On the due date for furnishing the return of income for that year.

question: If the Commissioner serves a demand notice after an assessment, how long do I have to pay?
reference_answer: Within thirty days of service of the notice.

question: Is income subject to salary withholding under section 149 included when computing quarterly advance tax under section 147?
reference_answer: No. Income subject to deduction at source under section 149 is excluded from the income on which section 147 advance tax is computed.

question: How does an employer calculate the tax to deduct from my monthly salary?
reference_answer: At the employee's average rate, computed on estimated salary income for the year at Division I, Part I, First Schedule rates (including section 4AB surcharge where applicable), after adjusting tax withheld under other heads and admissible tax credits.

question: Is tax deducted from pension paid to a retired employee?
reference_answer: Under section 149(1A), where pension to a former employee below 70 exceeds Rs. 10 million in a tax year, tax is deducted on the amount above Rs. 10 million at Division I rates, along with section 4AB tax.

question: How is withholding tax on dividends deducted?
reference_answer: The payer deducts tax from the gross dividend (or collects it on dividend in specie) at the rate in Division I of Part III of the First Schedule.

question: What is the general withholding rate on dividends, for example from a REIT?
reference_answer: 15% for Real Estate Investment Trusts and cases other than those specifically listed (Division I, Part III, First Schedule, clause (b)), for a recipient on the Active Taxpayers' List; for a recipient not on the list the rate is doubled under rule 1 of the Tenth Schedule, i.e. 30% (FBR rate card TY2027: 15% ATL, 30% non-ATL).

question: Who must deduct withholding tax on profit on debt under section 151?
reference_answer: Payers of yield on National Savings or Post Office accounts; banking companies and financial institutions on accounts or deposits; governments paying profit on securities; and other specified payers.

question: How is tax withheld on royalty or fees for technical services paid to a non-resident?
reference_answer: Where the royalty or fee for technical services is chargeable to tax under section 6, the payer deducts tax from the gross amount at the rate in Division IV of Part I of the First Schedule (section 152(1)).

question: Do I have to withhold tax when paying a supplier for goods worth less than Rs. 75,000 in total for the year?
reference_answer: No. Section 153(1)(a) does not apply where payments for goods are less than Rs. 75,000 in aggregate in a financial year.

question: Below what yearly total do payments for services escape withholding under section 153?
reference_answer: Payments for services below Rs. 30,000 in aggregate during a financial year.

question: How much tax is deducted on export proceeds of IT services for an exporter registered with PSEB?
reference_answer: The authorized dealer deducts 0.25% of the proceeds (for tax years 2024 to 2029) when the exporter is registered with and certified by the Pakistan Software Export Board. The tax is a final tax only if the conditions in section 154A(2) are met (return filed and withholding tax statements filed where required; the sales tax return condition does not apply to these exporters), and the exporter can opt out of final taxation each year (section 154A(3)).

question: What rate is deducted on export of services proceeds if the exporter is not registered with PSEB?
reference_answer: 1% of the proceeds ('any other case', Division IVA, Part III, First Schedule).

question: An individual landlord receives Rs. 500,000 rent a year. How much tax should the tenant withhold under section 155?
reference_answer: It depends on who the tenant is. Only a prescribed person must deduct tax from rent under section 155(1): the Federal Government, a Provincial Government, a Local Government, a company, a non-profit organization or charitable institution, a diplomatic mission of a foreign state, a private educational institution, boutique, beauty parlour, hospital, clinic or maternity home, an individual or association of persons paying gross rent of Rs. 1.5 million or more in a year, or any other person notified by the Board (section 155(3)). An ordinary individual tenant paying Rs. 500,000 a year is not a prescribed person and does not deduct tax. If the tenant is a prescribed person, serial 2 of Division V, Part III, First Schedule applies (rent above Rs. 300,000 and up to Rs. 600,000): 5% of the gross amount exceeding Rs. 300,000. 500,000 − 300,000 = 200,000; 5% x 200,000 = Rs. 10,000.

question: What is the withholding rate on rent paid to a company?
reference_answer: Tax is deducted only if the tenant is a prescribed person under section 155(3) (for example a government, a company, a non-profit organization, or an individual or association of persons paying gross rent of Rs. 1.5 million or more a year). Where it applies, the rate on rent paid to a company is 15% of the gross amount of rent (Division V, Part III, clause (b)) for a company on the Active Taxpayers' List, and 30% for one not on the list (FBR rate card TY2027: 15% ATL, 30% non-ATL, read with rule 1 of the Tenth Schedule).

question: How much tax is deducted on prize bond winnings, and is it final?
reference_answer: 15% of the gross amount paid for a winner on the Active Taxpayers' List (Division VI, Part III, First Schedule); for a winner not on the list the rate is doubled under rule 1 of the Tenth Schedule, i.e. 30% (FBR rate card TY2027: 15% ATL, 30% non-ATL). Under section 156(3) the tax is a final tax on the prize.

question: What is the tax rate on lottery, raffle or quiz winnings?
reference_answer: 20% of the gross amount paid (Division VI, Part III, First Schedule) for a winner on the Active Taxpayers' List; for a winner not on the list the rate is doubled under rule 1 of the Tenth Schedule, i.e. 40% (FBR rate card TY2027: 20% ATL, 40% non-ATL). Under section 156(3) the tax is a final tax on the winnings.

question: How can I stop tax being withheld from payments that are exempt or taxed at a lower rate?
reference_answer: Apply in writing (in the prescribed form) to the Commissioner for an exemption or lower rate certificate.

question: What happens if a withholding agent fails to deduct tax?
reference_answer: The person becomes personally liable to pay the tax to the Commissioner, who may pass an order and recover it after giving an opportunity of being heard.

question: How often must a withholding agent file withholding statements?
reference_answer: Quarterly, in the prescribed form.

question: Can I adjust tax deducted at source against my final tax liability?
reference_answer: Yes, in general: tax collected or deducted at source is treated as tax paid by the person, and a tax credit is allowed against the tax due for the tax year in which it was collected or deducted (sections 168(1) and 168(2)). The exception: no tax credit is allowed for tax collected or deducted that is a final tax under the provisions listed in section 168(3), for example tax on prizes and winnings under section 156(3). A credit that cannot be used in the year is refunded under section 170 (section 168(5)).

question: What does it mean when tax deducted is a 'final tax' under section 169?
reference_answer: The income is not chargeable under any head in computing taxable income, and no deduction is allowed for expenditure incurred in deriving it.

question: How long does the Commissioner have to decide my refund application?
reference_answer: Within sixty days of receiving the application, the Commissioner must serve a written order after giving an opportunity of being heard.

question: Do I get compensation if my tax refund is delayed?
reference_answer: Yes. If the refund is not paid within three months of becoming due, compensation is paid at KIBOR plus 0.5% per annum for the delay (section 171(1)). Exception: where there is reason to believe the refund claimed is not admissible, no compensation is paid until the investigation of the claim is completed and the claim is accepted or rejected (proviso to section 171(1)).

question: For how many years must a taxpayer keep accounts and records?
reference_answer: Six years after the end of the tax year they relate to, or until pending proceedings are finally decided.

question: Can an online marketplace let unregistered vendors sell on its platform?
reference_answer: No. Under section 181(1A) online marketplaces or courier services in e-commerce must not let a vendor use their platform unless the vendor is registered under the Ordinance.

question: Under which provision does FBR maintain the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: Section 181A empowers the Board to institute the active taxpayers' list, regulated as prescribed.

question: If an individual files the return after the due date, are they included in the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: Not for that year, unless they pay a surcharge on late filing: Rs. 25,000 for an individual (Rs. 50,000 for an AOP, Rs. 100,000 for a company). Under section 182A(3) the surcharge condition does not apply to an individual who gives the Commissioner an undertaking not to acquire any property for six months. A late filer also cannot carry forward a loss for that year and gets no refund while off the list.

question: Do I need an NTN to get a commercial electricity or gas connection?
reference_answer: Yes. An application for a commercial or industrial electricity or gas connection is not processed unless the applicant is registered under section 181.

question: What rate of default surcharge applies to tax paid late?
reference_answer: Twelve percent or KIBOR plus three percent per annum, whichever is higher, on the unpaid amount (advance tax under section 147 is excluded).

question: Who can apply for an advance ruling under the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: A non-resident taxpayer, by written application to the Board, about a proposed or completed transaction.

question: How much advance tax does a bank deduct on cash withdrawals by a person not on the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: 0.8% of cash withdrawals exceeding Rs. 50,000 in aggregate in a single day.

question: Is advance income tax collected on a domestic electricity bill if the consumer is on the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: No. The proviso to section 235(1) excludes a domestic consumer whose name appears on the Active Taxpayers' List.

question: Is advance income tax collected on internet bills and prepaid internet cards?
reference_answer: Yes, section 236 collects advance tax on telephone and internet bills and prepaid telephone and internet cards at Division V, Part IV rates. It is not collected from the Government, a foreign diplomat, a diplomatic mission in Pakistan, or a person who produces a Commissioner's certificate that his income for the tax year is exempt (section 236(4)).

question: How much advance tax does the seller pay when an immovable property is transferred?
reference_answer: The registering authority collects from the seller 2.75% of the gross consideration received (Division X, Part IV, First Schedule) if the seller is on the Active Taxpayers' List, and 11.5% if not (Tenth Schedule; FBR rate card TY2027). The tax is adjustable, but it is minimum tax if the property was acquired and disposed of in the same tax year, and it is a final discharge of tax liability (in lieu of capital gains tax) for a non-resident individual holding a POC, NICOP or CNIC who acquired the property through an FCVA or NRVA account; dependants of a Shaheed or of a person who died in government or armed forces service are exempt on the first sale of an allotted property (section 236C).

question: How much advance tax does a buyer pay when purchasing immovable property?
reference_answer: 1.25% of the fair market value for a purchaser on the Active Taxpayers' List, collected by the registering authority (Division XVIII, Part IV, First Schedule). A purchaser not on the list pays 10.5% where the fair market value does not exceed Rs. 50 million, 14.5% above Rs. 50 million up to Rs. 100 million, and 18.5% above Rs. 100 million (Tenth Schedule; FBR rate card TY2027). The tax is adjustable, except that it is a final discharge of tax liability for a non-resident individual holding a POC, NICOP or CNIC who buys through an FCVA or NRVA account (section 236K(2)); schemes of the Federal or a Provincial Government or authority for expatriate Pakistanis are excluded (section 236K(4)).

question: Is tax deducted when I pay a foreign merchant with my debit or credit card?
reference_answer: Yes. The bank collects advance tax when the amount is transferred abroad, at 0.5% of the gross amount remitted (Division XXVII, Part IV, First Schedule) for a person on the Active Taxpayers' List. For a person not on the list the rate is doubled under rule 1 of the Tenth Schedule, i.e. 1% (FBR rate card TY2027: 0.50% ATL, 1.00% non-ATL). The tax is adjustable (section 236Y(2)).

question: What capital gains tax rate applies to immovable property sold within one year of acquisition?
reference_answer: 15% where the holding period does not exceed one year (Division VIII, Part I). For property acquired on or after 1 July 2024, the 15% applies to persons on the Active Taxpayers' List on the date of disposal; persons not on the list pay at the Division I rates (individuals and AOPs) or Division II rates (companies), and for individuals and AOPs not on the list the rate is not less than 15% of the gain.

question: What capital gains tax applies to listed shares acquired after 1 July 2024 and sold by a person on the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: 15% for persons on the Active Taxpayers' List on the acquisition and disposal dates; for others, the Division I (individuals/AOPs) or Division II (companies) rates apply.

question: For tax year 2027, how much tax does a salaried individual (salary over 75% of taxable income) pay on taxable income of Rs. 1,000,000?
reference_answer: Rs. 1,000,000 exceeds Rs. 600,000 but does not exceed Rs. 1,200,000, so serial 2 of the salaried table (Division I, Part I, First Schedule) applies: 1% of the amount exceeding Rs. 600,000. 1,000,000 − 600,000 = 400,000; 1% x 400,000 = Rs. 4,000.

question: What is the top slab of income tax for non-salaried individuals and AOPs?
reference_answer: Taxable income above Rs. 5,600,000: Rs. 1,610,000 plus 45% of the amount above Rs. 5,600,000; the 45% is 40% for an AOP that is a professional firm prohibited from incorporating.

question: کیا ایک تنخواہ دار شخص جو ایک کروڑ روپے سے زیادہ کما رہا ہے اس کو سیکشن 4AB کے تحت سرچارج دینا ہوگا؟
reference_answer: No. The proviso to section 4AB says no surcharge is payable by an individual deriving income chargeable under the head 'Salary'.

question: اگر میرے پاس 500 مربع گز کے پلاٹ پر گھر ہے تو کیا ریٹرن جمع کرانا ضروری ہے، چاہے میری قابل ٹیکس آمدن نہ ہو؟

notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: Is agricultural income taxed under the Income Tax Ordinance?
reference_answer: No. Agricultural income derived by a person is exempt from tax under the Ordinance; it includes rent or revenue from, and income from agriculture on, land in Pakistan used for agricultural purposes.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: If a business later recovers an expense it already deducted, how is the recovered amount treated?
reference_answer: The amount received, in cash or in kind, is included in income chargeable under the same head for the tax year in which it is received.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: How is an expense that relates to more than one head of income treated?
reference_answer: It is apportioned on any reasonable basis, taking account of the relative nature and size of the activities to which it relates.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: Can a business deduct a fine or penalty it paid for breaking a law?
reference_answer: No. Any fine or penalty paid or payable for the violation of any law, rule or regulation is not deductible in computing business income.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: Are personal expenses deductible against business income?
reference_answer: No. Personal expenditures incurred by the person are not deductible in computing income from business.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: When is salary Pakistan-source income?
reference_answer: When it is received from employment exercised in Pakistan, wherever paid, or when it is paid by or on behalf of the Federal Government, a Provincial Government or a Local Government in Pakistan, wherever the employment is exercised.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: When is a dividend Pakistan-source income?
reference_answer: When it is paid by a resident company, or is a dividend under sub-clause (f) of clause (19) of section 2.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: What is the due date for a company's income tax return?
reference_answer: For a company whose tax year ends between 1 January and 30 June, on or before 31 December next following the end of the tax year; in any other case, on or before 30 September next following the end of the tax year.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: Does a person with salary income of Rs. 500,000 or more have to file the return electronically?
reference_answer: Yes. Where salary income for the tax year is Rs. 500,000 or more, the return must be filed electronically in the prescribed form, with proof of deduction or payment of tax and the wealth statement.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: Does a company or a non-profit organization have to file an income tax return even without taxable income?
reference_answer: Yes. Every company and every non-profit organization as defined in clause (36) of section 2 is required to furnish a return of income for a tax year.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: Can a person be required to file a return even if their income is below the taxable limit?
reference_answer: Yes. Among others, a person who was charged to tax for either of the two preceding tax years, or who claims a loss to be carried forward, must furnish a return.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: Does a widow or a non-resident have to file a return just because they own property?
reference_answer: No. A widow, an orphan below twenty-five years, a disabled person, and (for owning immovable property) a non-resident person are not required to furnish a return solely because of the property-ownership conditions of section 114(1)(b).
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: How can a taxpayer who cannot file the return by the due date get more time?
reference_answer: By applying in writing to the Commissioner by the due date. If the Commissioner is satisfied that the delay is due to absence from Pakistan, sickness or other misadventure, or any other reasonable cause, an extension may be granted, normally not exceeding fifteen days unless there are exceptional circumstances. Where the Commissioner has not granted an extension, the Chief Commissioner may, on the taxpayer's application, grant an extension or further extension, again not exceeding fifteen days unless there are exceptional circumstances (proviso to section 119(4)). An extension does not change the due date for paying the tax for the purpose of default surcharge (section 119(6)).
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: How much credit does a resident get for income tax paid abroad on foreign-source income?
reference_answer: A tax credit equal to the lesser of the foreign income tax paid and the Pakistan tax payable on that income, computed at the taxpayer's average rate of Pakistan tax on the net foreign-source income.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: What is pre-commencement expenditure, and how is it deducted?
reference_answer: Expenditure incurred before a business commences, wholly and exclusively to derive taxable income, such as feasibility studies, prototypes and trial production, but not land or depreciated or amortised costs. It is amortised on a straight-line basis at the rate in Part III of the Third Schedule.
notes: Adapted from an FBR publication; answer checked against the current Ordinance text (2026-06-30).

question: A shopkeeper pays Rs. 900,000 a year in rent to an individual landlord. Must the shopkeeper deduct tax from the rent under section 155?
reference_answer: No, unless the shopkeeper is a prescribed person under section 155(3). An individual paying gross rent below Rs. 1.5 million a year is a prescribed person only if the business is one of those listed (a private educational institution, boutique, beauty parlour, hospital, clinic or maternity home) or the person has been notified by the Board.
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).

question: My company rents an office from an individual for Rs. 800,000 a year. How much tax must the company deduct under section 155?
reference_answer: A company is a prescribed person (section 155(3)), so it must deduct tax. Rent of Rs. 800,000 falls in serial 3 of Division V, Part III, First Schedule: Rs. 15,000 plus 10% of the gross amount exceeding Rs. 600,000. 800,000 − 600,000 = 200,000; 10% x 200,000 = 20,000; 15,000 + 20,000 = Rs. 35,000.
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).

question: What is the withholding tax rate on a prize bond prize for a person who is not on the Active Taxpayers' List?
reference_answer: 30% of the gross amount paid: the 15% rate in Division VI, Part III, First Schedule is doubled under rule 1 of the Tenth Schedule for persons not on the Active Taxpayers' List (FBR rate card TY2027: 15% ATL, 30% non-ATL).
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).

question: Is a Federal Government officer who is posted abroad for the whole tax year a resident individual?
reference_answer: Yes. Under section 82(c) an employee or official of the Federal Government or a Provincial Government posted abroad in the tax year is a resident individual, even without 183 days of presence in Pakistan.
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).

question: Can I adjust the tax deducted on my prize bond winnings against my other income tax?
reference_answer: No. Under section 156(3) the tax deducted on prize bond prizes is a final tax on that income, and section 168(3) allows no tax credit for tax that is a final tax under section 156(3).
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).

question: I filed my return after the due date. Can I get onto the Active Taxpayers' List without paying the late-filing surcharge?
reference_answer: Normally the surcharge must be paid (Rs. 25,000 for an individual). But under section 182A(3) the surcharge condition does not apply to an individual who gives the Commissioner an undertaking not to acquire any property for six months from the date of the undertaking.
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).

question: How much advance tax does a buyer not on the Active Taxpayers' List pay on a property with a fair market value of Rs. 80 million?
reference_answer: 14.5% of the fair market value, the Tenth Schedule rate for a fair market value above Rs. 50 million and up to Rs. 100 million, instead of the 1.25% paid by persons on the Active Taxpayers' List (section 236K; FBR rate card TY2027).
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).

question: Is tax deducted on IT export proceeds of a PSEB-registered exporter always a final tax?
reference_answer: No. It is a final tax only if the conditions in section 154A(2) are met: the return has been filed and withholding tax statements have been filed where required (the sales tax return condition does not apply to PSEB-registered exporters). A person who does not meet the conditions, or opts out when filing the return each year, is not subject to final taxation (section 154A(3)).
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).

question: My only income is from a small business, Rs. 350,000 a year, which is below the taxable limit. Do I have to file a return?
reference_answer: Yes. Under section 114(1A) every individual whose income under the head Income from business exceeds Rs. 300,000 but does not exceed Rs. 400,000 in a tax year must also file a return of income.
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).

question: Does a non-resident who owns a 1,000 square yard plot in Pakistan have to file a return because of that plot?
reference_answer: No. Owning immovable property of 500 square yards or more normally requires a return under section 114(1)(b), but section 115(3)(d) says a non-resident person need not file solely because of owning immovable property.
notes: Added 2026-09-26 after the AI legal review: targets conditions and exceptions (D50).
